full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against an order dated 28.6.86 passed by Mr. Manjur Kader, Upazila Munsif, Banaripara in Title Suit No. 12 of 1985 refusing to dismiss the suit as being barred by res judicata. 

 2. Opposite party No. 1, namely, Abul Hashem Howlader being a plaintiff brought the suit praying for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in certain immovable property. One Audhor Chandra Barai, predecessor of the petitioners, was impleaded as defendant No. 1 therein. After being served with the summons the said defendant entered appearance and filed a written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit was barred by res judicata. He also filed an application praying for dismissal of the suit on that count. The application came up for hearing on 28.6.86. On that day the learned Munsif after hearing the parties and considering the materials placed before him took a view that the question of res judicata was irrelevant in the facts of the case and accordingly passed an order directing the issues to be framed, purporting to refuse the prayer of the defendant. Being aggrieved the petitioners who were in the meantime substituted in place of the deceased defendant No. 1. preferred an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure calling in question the propriety of the order and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Appearing on behalf of the petitioner Mr. Mujibur Rahman Talukder, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, urged that the learned Munsif committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in rejecting the application for dismissal of the suit as being barred by res judicata. According to him, opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff previously brought a suit being Title Suit No. 196 of 1984 seeking declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the disputed land and the same was dismissed on contest and since the said suit and the previous one are between the same parties and the matters in issue in the present suit were finally adjudicated in the previous suit, the present suit is barred by res judicata. 

 4. Mr. Tapan Kumar Chakraborty, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1, on the other hand, contends that the application which was filed by the defendant for dismissal of the suit was substantially one under Order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He argues that since the statements made in the plaint do not show that the suit is barred by any law the learned Munsif committed no illegality in refusing the prayer of the petitioner. It is further submitted by him that the question of res judicata can be considered only after the issues are framed in the suit and as the issues upon which the parties are contesting are yet to be framed, the learned Munsif was justified in passing the impugned order. 

 5. It appears that defendant No. 1 without getting the issues involved in the suits settled, preferred an application seeking dismissal of the suit as being barred by res judicata. The application is silent as to the provision under which it was filed. The learned Advocate for the petitioner frankly concedes that it was not filed as one under Order 14 rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure and so the question of res judicata could not be decided even as a preliminary issue at that stage. He, however, attempted to argue that the plaint was liable to be rejected under Clause (d) rule 11 of Order 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure as the Opposite Party No.1 as plaintiff earlier brought Title Suit No. 1 1984 against the petitioner and others praying declaration of his title and confirmation of possession in the disputed land which was decided on contest and as such matters in issue in both the suits are the same, the present suit is not maintainable. Clause (d) of rule 11 of Order 7 of the Code empowers the Court to reject a plaint if, on the face of statements made in the plaint, the suit is barred by any law. In exercising this power the court can look into the statements of the plaint only. It cannot consider any fact stated in the written statement or any document produced by the defendant. I have carefully perused the statements made in the plaint. There is nothing therein to conclusively hold that the suit is barred by any law. There is thus no substance in the submission of the learned advocate for the petitioner.
